newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on local cash buys.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Gas oil up on local cash buys.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps soared at midday on Wednesday following the emergence of a local trader on the physical market, firmer overnight crude prices and extended crude run cut at a Shell Singapore, traders said.
"The market was spooked after Hin Leong came out to buy last night," one trader said.
August gas oil swaps were last quoted up a hefty 50 cents from Tuesday at $23.05/$23.10. August traded earlier in the day at $22.95 and $23.00, brokers said.
The strong prompt interest has left September lagging with the August/September spread traded at minus 42 cents, compared to last week's trade of 48 cents, they said.
Traders said the market rose sharply because of the return of the Singapore trader, after an absence of about two months, to the physical market.
The trader, with two other companies, bought a total of over 18 million barrels in a buying spree that lasted about two months beginning March 3.
The buying binge led to sharp increase in spot Singapore prices which opened up a huge influx of arbitrage exports from the west totalling some three million tonnes.

The cargoes, which arrived from late May to early July, led to a slump in gas oil prices to a near two-year low with the market only now recovering as the system slowly absorbed the large arbitrage exports.
The Singapore trader on Tuesday bought 150,000-barrels at $22.85 per barrel for August 13-17 lifting with another cargo traded at $22.25 also same loading dates.
The local traders' willingness to buy at the higher level has led some players to speculate that the Singapore trader might just be the start of a new support wave.
Traders said prices were also lifted by Shell's decision to extend its crude run cut at its 435,000-barrel-per-day refinery into August.
Shell has cut output by almost 17-percent since June 27. Industy sources say Shell's August output cut will be less than the deep cuts made in July.
The jet fuel/gas oil spread or regrade narrowed further in response to the surging gas oil prices and lagging jet fuel fundamentals where there are by fears of a prompt overhang, traders said.
The August regrade was last quoted at flat/20 cents per barrel, down from 40/60 cents on Tuesday.
Fuel oil and naphtha was also quoted firmer in line with the stronger overnight crude. August was quoted up 50 cents at $99.75/$100.50 per tonne.
August naphtha was up 15 cents from Tuesday at $22.05/$22.25, brokers said.
